games.altBlowoutCheck: Bengals coming off a 38-18 win over PIT (margin 20, triggers the 17+ threshold): 1) Padded win - NO (led 24-3 at half, a 21-pt cushion, not within 8, and a 0-0 takeaway margin in the game); 2) Market bought in - YES (Bengals favored -6.5 vs WAS, >=3); 3) Opponent takes it away - YES (Washington ranks 7th in the NFL in takeaways forced, top 10); 4) Run-heavy win - NO (only 20 rush attempts); 5) Turnover-prone - YES (Bengals turnovers were the deciding factor in the Week 4 loss to Jacksonville, per contemporaneous coverage). 3 of 5 hit - regression flag ON: +6 to Washington Commanders.
games.altCategoryTally: Base 9-category: Bengals 6 - Commanders 1 (Injuries/Lineup weighted x2 for Bengals). Plus blowout-regression check +6 Commanders. Trend check +0. Final combined: Bengals 6 - Commanders 7 -> net Commanders +1 (combined lead <=3 => pass)
altReasons: Scoring margin: favors Bengals (blended PD/g +2.4 vs -4.3). No major-QB-change discount applies to either team: Burrow has started all 9 Bengals games this season, and Daniels - despite missing Weeks 3-4 with an elbow injury (Mariota started those two) - returned in Week 5 and has made 6 consecutive starts since, so neither team's PD/g was built mostly under a different QB than tonight's starter.
Rest: favors Commanders (Washington played a Thursday night game on 11/12, giving it 11 days of rest into this Monday game, versus Cincinnati's standard 8-day turnaround off its Sunday 11/15 win).
Travel: neutral (both teams based on the East Coast; no time-zone change, cross-country trip, or international site).

Injuries/Lineup: favors Bengals, weighted x2 - multi-starter cluster (Commanders are missing two premium-position starters: WR1 Terry McLaurin, out for the season with a knee injury, and starting LT Laremy Tunsil, on injured reserve after triceps surgery (ESPN lists an estimated 20 Dec return; HC Dan Quinn says there is no timetable) - out for this game either way. Bengals are missing only one premium starter, starting RG Dalton Risner (knees), with backup Jalen Rivers starting in his place - a single-starter injury, not a cluster).

Form (last 3 games): favors Bengals (Cincinnati is 3-0 in its last three: 43-36 OT over Titans, 34-17 over Falcons, 38-18 over Steelers. Washington is 2-1: beat Eagles 27-10 and Giants 24-21, lost to Rams 13-20. No major-QB-change discount applies, same reasoning as Scoring margin above.)

Motivation/Spot: neutral (Cincinnati is protecting a 5-game win streak and the AFC North lead; Washington is in a near-must-win spot to stay in the playoff picture, and HC Dan Quinn is reported to be on the hot seat over an 8-game stretch - motivation cuts both ways with no single clear checkable edge).
Weather/Venue: neutral (forecast for Landover, MD is clear and mild - upper 50s at kickoff, 10% precipitation chance; no wind, cold, altitude, or venue factor in play).

Market: favors Bengals (the spread firmed from roughly Bengals -5.5/-6 earlier in the week to Bengals -6.5 by game week, with one outlet explicitly noting 'Cincy gaining massive momentum as favorite' - money has moved toward, not away from, the favorite).
Matchup splits: favors Bengals (Cincinnati's No. 1-ranked passing offense, 298.8 YPG, lines up directly against Washington's 31st-ranked pass defense, 244.8 YPG allowed).

games.thirdReasoning: Cincinnati's offensive explosion (five straight 30+ point games, NFL-best completion rate) against the league's 31st-ranked pass defense is the dominant signal, compounded by Washington's absence of both its left tackle and WR1. That's offset by two real counter-signals: Washington gets extra rest off a Thursday game, and Cincinnati's own blowout-win profile (a lopsided, takeaway-less win last week, plus a turnover-cost loss earlier this season) argues against assuming a repeat blowout margin. Net, I project a comfortable but not overwhelming Bengals win that clears the number by only a few points. The most surprising angle: Washington's offense (28th in rush EPA, 33% on third down) may struggle to generate any backdoor points of its own, which is what tips this from a 'pass' into a lean on Cincinnati rather than a true coin-flip. A sloppy Burrow turnover game or an early offensive-line breakdown for Cincinnati would flip this.
thirdResearch: [angle] Commanders HC Dan Quinn is squarely on the hot seat entering this stretch - Washington media have flagged an upcoming multi-game stretch as a referendum on his job security after a 3-5-1 start, raising the stakes of a nationally televised home game (atozsports.com, riggosrag.com, Nov 2026).

[angle] Washington's offensive line was reshuffled this week: with LT Laremy Tunsil on injured reserve (triceps surgery; est. return 20 Dec per ESPN) and C Lucas Patrick in concussion protocol (Nick Allegretti likely starting at center), the Commanders are breaking in new line combinations against a Cincinnati pass rush (ClutchPoints Week 11 preview).

[angle] WR1 Terry McLaurin is out for the rest of the season (knee surgery), leaving Stefon Diggs (386 yards, 6 TDs) as Washington's clear top target - a thinner receiving corps facing a Bengals secondary that, while mediocre overall, has size on the outside.

Joe Burrow leads the NFL in completion percentage (74.7%) with 27 TDs against just 6 INTs through 9 games, and Cincinnati has scored 30-plus points in every game of its current 5-game winning streak (capperspicks.com, covers.com).

Washington's pass defense ranks 31st in the league (244.8 YPG allowed), a direct mismatch against Cincinnati's No. 1-ranked passing offense (298.8 YPG) built around Ja'Marr Chase (878 yds, 7 TD) and Tee Higgins (824 yds, 6 TD), both expected to play at full health.

Washington's own offense ranks 28th in rush EPA and has converted only 33.3% of third downs this season, limiting its ability to sustain long, clock-eating drives even against a middling Bengals defense (23rd in EPA/play, 25th in rush EPA).

[angle] Washington gets extra rest: its Week 10 game fell on Thursday 11/12, giving it 11 days before this Monday kickoff, versus Cincinnati's standard 8-day turnaround off its Sunday 11/15 win - a scheduling edge for Washington's banged-up roster to recover.

Washington's defense does have playmakers: Odafe Oweh has 5 sacks and CB Rasul Douglas has 3 interceptions this season, giving the Commanders some ability to disrupt Burrow and create a short field even while ranking poorly overall on defense.

Spread trend: Cincinnati has covered 3 of its last 4 games as a favorite; its lone miss came as a 13.5-point favorite in a 43-36 overtime shootout win over Tennessee, showing the Bengals' defense can get shaky even in wins when games turn into track meets.

Spread trend: Washington is 5-4 against the spread this season and has held three of its last four opponents to 21 points or fewer, though it also managed only 13 points of its own in a Week 9 loss to the Rams - offensive inconsistency that cuts both ways for a backdoor-cover profile.

Line movement: the spread opened in roughly the Bengals -5.5/-6 range earlier in the week and firmed to Bengals -6.5 by game week, with one outlet explicitly describing 'Cincy gaining massive momentum as favorite' - money has moved toward, not away from, the favorite.

[angle] Cincinnati's blowout-win regression profile: the Bengals' 38-18 win over Pittsburgh was built on a 21-point halftime lead with zero takeaways gained (not a stat-padded or turnover-fueled score), and turnovers were specifically cited as the deciding factor in Cincinnati's Week 4 loss to Jacksonville - a reminder that Burrow's ball security, while good overall, has been the difference in a loss before.

Cincinnati's run defense has allowed touchdowns on 40% of opponents' red-zone trips this season and ranks 25th in rush EPA - a soft spot Washington could lean on with Jayden Daniels' legs (280 rushing yards this season) to manufacture points even if the Commanders can't sustain drives through the air.

Weather is a non-factor: Monday night forecast for Landover calls for a clear, mild evening (upper 50s at kickoff, 10% precipitation chance), removing any wind/rain equalizer that might have helped Washington's ground game or hurt Cincinnati's passing attack.
